transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’ve started to feel like I’m just not good enough at anything anymore, no matter how hard I try. My husband actually encouraged me to come in and talk to someone because it's been weighing on me so much lately.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful or upsetting event, or have they come on without any clear trigger? How long have you been feeling this way?

It really started a little over two years ago, when my husband and I began fertility treatments and I took on extra responsibilities mentoring new teachers at school. This heavy, low mood has been pretty much continuous since then, and it feels like I've just been dragging myself through life.
Since these feelings began, have you had periods of at least a couple of months when your mood felt back to normal, or has it been low most of the time without a break?

No, I haven't had any breaks where I felt back to normal. This heavy, dragging feeling has been constant almost every single day for a little over two years, ever since we started the fertility treatments. It just never really lifts.

Did your symptoms begin only after the fertility treatments and added work stress, and do they feel mainly tied to those stressors? Or did they start without a clear trigger and just persist on their own?

They definitely started shortly after we began the fertility treatments and I took on the extra mentoring work at school. At first, it felt tied to those specific disappointments and pressures, but over time it has turned into a continuous, heavy feeling that just persists on its own every day. Now, it feels like I'm just stuck in this loop no matter what.
Do your symptoms mainly come and go in response to the fertility and work stress, or have they stayed present most days even when things are relatively calm?

They don't really come and go; this heavy, low mood stays with me most days, even when things are calm or when something good happens. It has been continuous like this for a little over two years now, and it just never seems to lift.

Did your symptoms begin only after the fertility/work stress and stay tied to those stressors, or did they continue for months even when the stressors were no longer present? Two or more months of feeling mostly back to normal would be especially important to know.

They started with those stressors, but they have continued constantly regardless of whether things are busy or quiet. I definitely haven't had any periods of two months, or even a few weeks, where I felt back to normal. It has just been an ongoing, daily struggle without any real breaks for over two years.
Have you also had symptoms like intrusive memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or being constantly on edge related to the fertility treatments or work stress?

No, I don't have any nightmares, flashbacks, or feel constantly on edge like that. It's more of a constant, heavy sadness and feeling completely drained, along with this nagging feeling that I'm just failing at everything.
Have you been avoiding reminders of the fertility treatments or work stress, or felt jumpy, hypervigilant, or easily startled since this started?

No, I don't feel jumpy, hypervigilant, or easily startled at all, and I don't really avoid reminders in that way. I have started avoiding family gatherings, but that is simply because of emotional exhaustion and wanting to avoid painful questions about having children. It's more about just not having the energy to face everyone.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months since this started when you felt mostly back to your usual self, even if the stressors were still present?

No, I haven't had any period of two months—or even close to that—where I felt back to my usual self. This heavy, low mood and feeling of dragging myself through life has been pretty much continuous and constant ever since it started a little over two years ago. There just hasn't been any real break or relief from it.
Have you had any intrusive memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or feeling constantly on edge since this started?
No, I haven't really experienced nightmares, flashbacks, or feeling constantly on edge. My experience is much more about feeling exhausted, empty, and low rather than anxious or startled in that way.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months since this started when you felt mostly back to your usual self, even if the stressors were still present?

No, I really haven't had any break like that at all. Since this started over two years ago, the heavy mood and lack of energy have been completely continuous. I haven't had a period of two months, or even a few weeks, where I felt like my usual self again.
Did your low mood and exhaustion start within a month of the fertility/work stressors, or did they begin later and keep going even after the stressors changed?

Yes, those feelings started pretty much within a month of us starting the fertility treatments and me taking on the extra mentoring workload. Since then, it has been a continuous, heavy presence for over two years now, and it hasn't let up at all even as time has gone on.
When the fertility and work stressors improved or changed, did your mood and energy improve too, or did the low mood continue even when those stressors were no longer present?

The fertility struggles and work pressures have actually been ongoing over these past two years, but the heavy, low mood and low energy have remained completely continuous. Even during brief moments of relief or when something objectively good happens at school, that heavy feeling never really lifts. It just stays with me constantly, regardless of how those stressors are going.

Did your symptoms start within a month of the stressful events, and have they stayed mainly tied to those stressors rather than continuing on their own? Also, have you had any clear periods of feeling back to normal for at least two months since this began?

Yes, they started shortly after the fertility treatments and extra work began about two years ago, but now it feels like a constant, independent cloud rather than just being tied to those events. I definitely haven't had any periods of feeling back to normal for two months; this low mood has been completely continuous since it started.
Have you had any symptoms of anxiety or trauma-related stress, such as intrusive memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or feeling constantly on edge since this started?

No, I haven't really experienced any of those symptoms, like nightmares, flashbacks, or feeling constantly on edge. It's just been that heavy, drained feeling and the constant sadness I've already described.
Have you also had other depression symptoms, such as losing interest or pleasure in things, changes in sleep or appetite, poor concentration, low energy, or thoughts that life is not worth living?

I feel completely drained all the time, and no matter how much I sleep, I just collapse on the couch as soon as I get home from school. I've definitely lost interest in things and have started withdrawing, like turning down our Sunday family dinners and avoiding my friends. I don't have any thoughts of ending my life, but the sheer physical and emotional exhaustion is just overwhelming.
Have you been sleeping much more than usual, or is your sleep mostly normal but you still feel exhausted?

No matter how much sleep I get, I still feel completely drained and exhausted all the time. By the end of the school day I have to force myself to stay upbeat for the kids, and when I get home I just collapse on the couch because even simple chores like loading the dishwasher feel like too much effort.
Have you ever had any earlier periods of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things, or has this been the first and only episode?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before; this is the first and only time I've ever felt this kind of depression or loss of interest. It all started about two years ago when we began the fertility treatments and I took on the extra work at school, and before that, I had never felt this way.
Have you felt depressed or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time during this episode?

Yes, it has been much longer than two weeks—it's been a constant, heavy sadness nearly every day for over two years since we started fertility treatments. I've also lost interest in things I used to enjoy, like going to Sunday family dinners or seeing friends, simply because I don't have the energy to be present anymore.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months during the past two years when your mood and interest felt back to normal, or has the depression been present most of the time without a real break?

No, I haven't had any real breaks at all. This heavy, low-grade sadness has been there pretty much continuously for the past two years since we started fertility treatments. I definitely haven't had any period where things felt back to normal.

Have you had any changes in appetite, sleep, concentration, or feelings of hopelessness during this time? These can help tell whether this is a major depressive episode or a more chronic low mood condition.

I definitely feel a deep sense of hopelessness—I just can't picture the future getting any better and feel like I'm stuck in this loop forever. Sleep-wise, no matter how much I get, I still feel constantly drained and exhausted every single day. I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite or concentration, though.
During the past two years, have you ever had a period of at least two months when your mood and interest in things felt mostly back to normal?

No, I haven't had any period of two months where I felt back to normal. This heavy, low mood has been completely continuous and hasn't given me any real break since it started a little over two years ago.
Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energetic or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or felt more confident or impulsive than normal?

No, I have never experienced a period of feeling unusually energetic, hyperactive, or needing less sleep. My experience has actually been the complete opposite. I just feel constantly drained, tired, and low all the time.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months in the past two years when you felt mostly back to your usual self, or has the low mood been present nearly every day without a real break?

No, I haven't had any break at all, and the low mood has been present nearly every day. This heavy, dragging feeling has been continuous for a little over two years since we started fertility treatments. I definitely haven't had a period of two months or more where I felt back to my usual self.
Besides feeling sad and exhausted, have you lost interest or pleasure in most things you usually enjoy, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

It's not so much that I've lost interest in the things I enjoy, but rather that I feel too exhausted, drained, and overwhelmed to actually participate in them. I also end up withdrawing from things like family dinners just to avoid uncomfortable questions, because I simply don't have the emotional energy to face them.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 years where you felt depressed or down most days, but not as intensely as a major depression, with no symptom-free period longer than 2 months?

Yes, that is exactly what I've been experiencing. This heavy, low mood and dragging feeling has been present pretty much continuously for a little over two years, ever since we started fertility treatments. There haven't been any real breaks or periods where that sadness lifted.
Have you ever had any period of at least 2 months during the past 2 years when your mood felt mostly back to normal, or has it been low nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any period of normal mood lasting that long at all. This heavy, low mood and the feeling of dragging myself through life has been there pretty much continuously, nearly every day, for the entire two years since we started fertility treatments. There has been absolutely no real break or return to normal during this whole time.
During this time, have you had several other depression symptoms most days as well, such as major changes in appetite or weight, slowed down or agitated movements, or trouble concentrating?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes in my appetite or weight, and my concentration seems to be mostly okay. I also haven't experienced any of those slowed down or agitated movements you mentioned.

Over the past two years, have you had several other depression symptoms most days, such as major changes in appetite or weight, sleep problems, low energy, poor concentration, or feelings of worthlessness or guilt?

Yes, I have definitely struggled with constant low energy and strong feelings of worthlessness and guilt over the past two years. I feel completely drained no matter how much I sleep, and there is this running commentary in my head telling me I'm a bad wife and a mediocre teacher. I haven't really noticed major changes in my appetite, but the exhaustion and those negative thoughts are there almost every day.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months in the past 2 years when your mood and energy felt mostly back to normal, or has it been low nearly every day without a real break?

No, I haven't had any breaks or periods where I felt back to normal. This heavy, low mood and low energy have been dragging me down pretty much continuously, nearly every single day, ever since we started fertility treatments a little over two years ago.
